flags: USB-C look-alike trap: only one of the four USB-C upstream ports carries video (DisplayPort Alt Mode, up to 90W PD); the other three are data-only KVM ports per Dell's port list.
Factory-calibration claim: Dell's spec table lists Calibration Accuracy Delta E < 2.
Speakers are 2x 8W per Dell's spec table.
Dell lists the HDMI 2.1 ports as TMDS; DisplayPort and the USB-C video port are the full-bandwidth paths.
Dell publishes no DCI-P3 coverage for this model (95% sRGB) despite the UltraSharp creator branding.

inputs.usbc_note: TRUE USB-C VIDEO INPUT on one port: USB-C upstream with DisplayPort 1.4 Alt Mode and Power Delivery up to 90W. TRAP: three additional USB-C upstream ports are data-only (for KVM switching) and carry no video. Hub also includes 4x USB-A downstream, 1x USB-C downstream (15W) and an RJ45 Ethernet port (1GbE).

name: Dell UltraSharp 43 4K USB-C Hub Monitor - U4323QE
quality_basis: High pixel density for its size (103.6 ppi) with an IPS panel; Dell publishes 95% sRGB only, with no DCI-P3 figure, so it does not meet the 'color' band's wide-gamut evidence standard.
refresh_note: 60Hz native at 3840x2160 per Dell spec; no overclock figure published.
why: A 42.5-inch 4K IPS screen that is also the dock: real USB-C video with 90W charging, KVM, Ethernet and built-in speakers, so one big panel can replace a dual-monitor setup.

flags: Two look-alike upstream ports: Thunderbolt 4 (video + data, up to 140W charging) and a separate USB-C upstream that Dell specifies as data only. Plugging the laptop into the USB-C port gives a black screen.
Brightness is 450 cd/m2 typical; the 600 cd/m2 figure is HDR peak only.
Factory calibration: Dell's What's Included lists a factory calibration report, and the gamut spec states Delta E < 2 (average) across DCI-P3, Display P3, sRGB and BT.709.
Speakers are 2x 9W per Dell's spec table; curvature is 2500R.
Retailer spec error: Micro Center's spec block lists the aspect ratio as 16:9; Dell's spec table says 21:9 (5120x2160).
Price spread: Dell's own US listing data showed $2,399.99 / Sold Out when crawled, while Micro Center showed $1,899.99 in stock on the check date; the Micro Center price is recorded.

inputs.usbc_note: TRUE THUNDERBOLT VIDEO INPUT: Thunderbolt 4 upstream is specified by Dell as Video + Data with DisplayPort 1.4 Alt Mode and Power Delivery up to 140W EPR; a Thunderbolt 4 downstream port (15W) supports daisy-chaining. TRAP: a separate USB-C upstream port is data-only (SuperSpeed USB 10 Gbps, USB 3.2 Gen 2) and carries no video. Hub adds 5x USB-A downstream, 2x USB-C downstream (15W) and an RJ45 Ethernet port (2.5GbE).

name: Dell UltraSharp 40 Curved Thunderbolt Hub Monitor - U4025QW
quality_basis: Top published gamut (99% DCI-P3) plus a spec'd HDR class (VESA DisplayHDR 600); factory calibration report included per Dell.
refresh_note: 120Hz native at 5120x2160 per Dell spec (DisplayPort 1.4 with DSC, HDMI 2.1 FRL, or Thunderbolt 4).
why: The widescreen dock flagship: 5K2K IPS Black at 120Hz with 99% DCI-P3, DisplayHDR 600, Thunderbolt 4 with up to 140W charging, KVM and 2.5GbE Ethernet in one curved 40-inch panel.

flags: USB-C trap: the USB-C port is an upstream data link for the USB hub only - Samsung's interface list has video only via DisplayPort, HDMI and Micro HDMI. It is not a video input and offers no meaningful laptop charging.
VESA mounting needs the included adapter bracket - the back panel has no native VESA holes (confirmed by Samsung's own answer in the Best Buy Q&A).
Brightness is 250 cd/m2 typical (200 min); the roughly 1,000-nit HDR figure is a small-window (3% APL) peak.
No KVM switch in Samsung's spec table, so one keyboard/mouse set cannot be switched between two computers the way the Dell hub monitors do it.
Built-in speakers are fitted; Samsung's spec table does not headline a wattage.

Spec-sourcing note: Samsung's US product page could not be fetched during the sweep; values are from Samsung's published spec table/manual for the G93SD series and Samsung's regional product page, cross-checked against the Best Buy listing.

inputs.usbc_note: USB-C TRAP: data-only upstream link for the USB hub - no DisplayPort Alt Mode video and no meaningful power delivery. Video is via DisplayPort, HDMI or Micro HDMI only.

name: Samsung Odyssey OLED G9 (G93SD) - LS49DG934SNXGO
quality_basis: OLED panel (QD-OLED) per Samsung's spec table; premium rests on the OLED rule - Samsung lists HDR10/HDR10+ Gaming but no VESA DisplayHDR class for this model.
refresh_note: 240Hz native at 5120x1440 per Samsung spec; 0.03ms response time; 1800R curvature.
why: Two 27-inch QHD screens fused into one 49-inch QD-OLED with no center bezel: 240Hz, 0.03ms and 99% DCI-P3 for racing, flight sims and sprawling timelines.

flags: Gamut trap avoided: ASUS publishes no DCI-P3 coverage percentage for this model - it offers a DCI-P3 preset mode only. Published gamut is 100% sRGB (overview also states 100% Rec.709), so dci_p3_percent is null, not a guess.
60Hz panel: this is a creator/docking pick, not a high-refresh gaming monitor.
No KVM switch in ASUS's spec table (PIP/PBP only), despite the docking feature set.
Speakers are 2W x2 per the ASUS spec table.
HDMI ports are v2.0; fine for 3440x1440 at 60Hz, but there is no HDMI 2.1 headroom.

inputs.displayport: DisplayPort 1.4 x2 (1 in, 1 out for MST daisy-chaining)
inputs.usbc_note: TRUE USB-C VIDEO INPUT: USB-C x1 with DisplayPort Alt Mode, data and Power Delivery up to 96W. The hub adds 1x USB-C and 2x USB-A downstream (USB 3.2 Gen 1) plus an RJ45 Ethernet port.

name: ASUS ProArt Display PA34VCNV
quality_basis: Factory-calibration claim in the spec sheet (Calman Verified, factory pre-calibrated Delta E < 2, calibration report included).
refresh_note: 60Hz maximum per ASUS spec; no overclock figure published. 3800R curvature.
why: The creator ultrawide value pick: factory-calibrated IPS with Delta E < 2, 100% sRGB and Rec.709, a 96W USB-C dock with Ethernet and daisy-chaining, at a mid-range price.

flags: Retailer spec errors: Best Buy's spec block lists 'Panel Type: IPS' for this OLED monitor, and labels the gamut 'Color Gamut (NTSC) 98.5 percent' - LG's spec is an OLED panel with DCI-P3 98.5%.
USB-C wattage contradiction on the same Best Buy page: 65W in the product description versus 90W in LG-supplied feature copy. LG's own materials say 90W; 90W is recorded.
The DisplayPort 2.1 port is UHBR13.5 (54 Gbps), not full UHBR20 - full 5120x2160 at 165Hz with 10-bit HDR needs DSC (per LG's own support answer in the Best Buy Q&A).
Brightness is 275 cd/m2 typical; the headline 1,300-nit figure is a small-window peak.

Price spread: a Best Buy Marketplace listing (sold and shipped by Beach Camera) showed $1,299.99, while Best Buy's own listing showed $1,999.99 on the check date; the Best Buy direct price is recorded.
Marketed as 45-inch; the viewable panel is 44.5 inches per LG's spec.
Speakers are 10W x2 per LG's spec table; 800R curvature.

inputs.usbc_note: TRUE USB-C VIDEO INPUT: USB-C x1 carries video, data and Power Delivery (90W per LG's spec; the retailer page contradicts itself at 65W in one section - see flags). Hub adds 2x USB-A 3.0 downstream.

name: LG UltraGear 45GX950A-B
quality_basis: OLED panel per LG's spec table (also 98.5% DCI-P3 with a spec'd HDR class, VESA DisplayHDR True Black 400).
refresh_note: 165Hz native at 5120x2160; Dual Mode switches to 2560x1080 at 330Hz. 0.03ms response time.
why: The biggest OLED canvas here: a 45-inch-class 5K2K panel at 165Hz (or 330Hz in Dual Mode) with DisplayHDR True Black 400 and 98.5% DCI-P3 - a sim cockpit and a giant editing desk in one.
